watches.name: Firestarter
watches.description: Firestarter is the first watch from Pinion’s new Foundation collection. Built in batches of 100, it combines a new 38mm stainless steel case and high-domed sapphire crystal with a vibrant natural Red Agate stone dial. Inside is the Japanese Miyota 9039 automatic movement. Each Firestarter is designed, assembled, regulated and tested in England by Pinion founder Piers Berry, who remains closely connected to the watch from first sketch to final regulation. watches.name: Neutron Dual RD
watches.description: The Pinion Neutron® Dual features a red electroplated dial with an engine-turned centre displaying a second 24-hour time zone. Housed in a 38 mm stainless steel case and powered by the robust Swiss ETA 2893-2 automatic movement, each watch is designed, assembled and tested by hand in England. View full specifications Price includes VAT and delivery. VAT portion: £ 225.00 . 38mm 100 metres Automatic 20mm Dual Precision Designed and built in England, the Neutron Dual expands on the design language of the original Neutron, adding true dual-time functionality in the same compact 38 mm case. It’s powered by the dependable Swiss ETA 2893-2 automatic movement and features a beautifully detailed electroplated dial – an elegant balance of precision, design and purpose. Big on details The Neutron Dual’s dial is a showcase of craft and clarity, with an engine-turned centrepiece framed by a brushed outer ring and finished in rich electroplated colour. Polished nickel numerals are applied by hand, while printed batons filled with Super-LumiNova give a subtle glow in low light. In keeping with Pinion’s understated style, the logo sits quietly on the inner rehaut, letting the dial’s textures take centre stage. Second 24-hour time zone The Dual adds a second configurable 24-hour time zone (often referred to as a GMT) making it ideal for wearers who want to track multiple time zones. The hour and minute hands track local time, while the subtle 24-hour hand can be independently set via the crown to another time zone. At a glance, both times are instantly readable – a practical complication crafted in refined simplicity. Inside view Powering the Neutron Dual is the top-grade Swiss ETA 2893-2 automatic movement, chosen for its reliability and smooth operation. Through the sapphire exhibition case back, the movement is revealed – complete with a custom Pinion rotor finished in hunter green. This practical mechanism winds itself as you move, keeping the watch running with effortless precision while offering a glimpse into its finely finished mechanical workings. Made in small batches Like every Pinion watch, the Neutron Dual is produced in small numbers and built by hand in England. This approach means every watch receives the care and attention it deserves before it leaves the workshop. Specifications Dimensions Diameter 38mm (excluding crown) Length 45mm Strap 20mm Depth 11mm (including glass) Weight 55g (75g with leather strap) Movement ETA 2893-2 Automatic (self-winding mechanism) 28’800 vibrations per hour (4 Hz) 21 Jewels 42 hours (typical) power reserve Date All models have the date wheel and setting mechanism removed Accuracy Regulated in-house to 3-positions (dial-up, dial-down, crown-down) +/- 5 seconds to +/- 15 seconds per day accuracy Case Water resistance 100 metres / 10 ATM Material Stainless steel, brushed finish Case back Solid engraved case back, brushed finish Crown Push-down with double o-ring fitting Glass Domed sapphire with anti-reflective coating (inside only) Details Dial Electroplated with circular brushed finish. Central engine-turned decoration. Polished applied numerals. Hands Coated brass hands in polished finish with contrasting etched groove (hour, minutes) Luminance Swiss Super-LumiNova ‘old radium’ applied to dial batons and hands with green luminance

Housed in a 42mm stainless steel case and powered by the reliable Swiss Sellita SW200-1 automatic movement, each watch is hand-built, regulated and tested in England for precision and durability. View full specifications Watch is pictured on Warm grey Badalassi wax strap (Please note: the current batch of these straps are darker in tone than pictured here). Note: See our help page for more information on Sellita and LGP Movements 42mm 100 METRES AUTOMATIC 22MM Bold renewal The Reaxis reimagines one of Pinion’s original designs — the Axis — bringing it back with a new burst of energy and colour. Sized at 42mm and powered by the dependable Swiss Sellita SW200-1 automatic movement, the Reaxis introduces five vibrant dial colours that capture light and movement beautifully. Each watch is hand-built, regulated and tested in England, combining bold design with the craftsmanship and reliability expected of every Pinion timepiece.> Colour burst At the heart of the Reaxis is a dial that plays with light and motion. Its brushed sunburst texture radiates from the centre, shifting and shimmering as your wrist moves. Each dial is electroplated to achieve its rich tone — available in magenta, anthracite, blue, green or red — creating dynamic bursts of colour that change with every glance. Circular applied indexes, polished and electroplated by hand, add clarity and depth to the design, staying true to Pinion’s signature aesthetic. After Glow The Reaxis is designed to shine day or night, thanks to its use of Super-LumiNova® C3. This mythical symbol of renewal and transformation captures the spirit of the Reaxis itself — a rebirth of one of Pinion’s earliest designs. The phoenix’s vibrant energy echoes through the collection’s colourful dials, linking the artistry on the case back with the life and light on the front. Durable and Robust The 42mm case is crafted from 316L stainless steel, with a seamless two-part design that blends the bezel into the main body for a clean, balanced look. The circular brushed top and domed sapphire crystal give it both strength and refinement, while the anti-reflective coating ensures perfect clarity. Inside, the Swiss Sellita SW200-1 automatic movement provides reliable precision and is regulated in England across three positions for accuracy within ±5 seconds a day. watches.name: Elapse Anthracite (TWC)
watches.description: The Pinion Elapse AN (Anthracite) Chronograph. 42mm stainless steel watch. Powered by a Swiss automatic movement (Valjoux 7750). Electroplated dial, in a vertically brushed finish. Matt nickle hands with Super Luminova BG W9. Designed, finished, assembled and tested in England. 42mm 100 metres Automatic 22mm Presenting the Elapse. Pinion’s first automatic chronograph that is powered by the world-renowned Valjoux 7750 movement. Sized at 42mm in diameter, as the name indicates, will allow the wearer to track elapsed time in seconds, minutes and hours, controlled by the two polished steel pushers. As with all Pinion watches, the Elapse is built in small batches in England and comes with a two-year warranty. Track elapsed time The two polished chronograph pushers enable the wearer to start and stop intervals of elapsed time, which is observed from the registers and central chronograph seconds hand. A simple push of the upper button starts the chronograph running. Pressing the same button again will pause it so elapsed time can be read. The wearer can then reset the chronograph by pushing the lower button or continue to track intervals of time with start/stop from the upper button. The elapse captures 60 seconds from the central chronograph seconds. Every revolution moves the register at 12H to capture up-to 30 minutes. Longer durations of elapsed time of up to 12 hours can be read from the register at 6H. A world-leading mechanical movement Originally made in the early 1970s, the Valjoux 7750 is an updated automatic version of its hand-wound predecessors, the 7733 line from the sixties (which featured in Pinion’s R1969 limited edition chronograph). Since then, the Valjoux 7750 movement has been widely utilised by many watch companies and has become known worldwide as a simple, rugged and efficient movement. A cam-shifting action triggers the process of stopping and starting the chronograph, and the sizeable automatic winding rotor can create a characteristic known as the ‘7750 wobble’ when worn. Electroplated dial Several processes are undertaken on the dial to give its multi-contrast finish. First, the chronograph registers are milled at 12H and 6H to create two lower levels. Engine turning is applied to these to create a contrasting effect making them appear darker under differing lighting conditions. Next, subtle vertical brushing is applied to the base of the dial and circular brushing to the outer rehault ring. These are then electroplated with colour. The brushing helps with the contrasting tone of colour when viewed in different lighting conditions. Finally, the dials are gently buffed before printing commences. Once complete, a galvanic varnish is applied, sealing the elements and providing a glossy surface to the dial. watches.description: The Pinion Elapse SI (Silver) Chronograph. 42mm stainless steel watch. Powered by a Swiss automatic movement (Valjoux 7750). Electroplated dial, in a vertically brushed finish. Blued hands with Super Luminova BG W9. Designed, finished, assembled and tested in England Presenting the Elapse. Pinion’s first automatic chronograph that is powered by the world-renowned Valjoux 7750 movement. Sized at 42mm in diameter, as the name indicates, will allow the wearer to track elapsed time in seconds, minutes and hours, controlled by the two polished steel pushers. As with all Pinion watches, the Elapse is built in small batches in England and comes with a two-year warranty. Track elapsed time The two polished chronograph pushers enable the wearer to start and stop intervals of elapsed time, which is observed from the registers and central chronograph seconds hand. A simple push of the upper button starts the chronograph running. Pressing the same button again will pause it so elapsed time can be read. The wearer can then reset the chronograph by pushing the lower button or continue to track intervals of time with start/stop from the upper button. The elapse captures 60 seconds from the central chronograph seconds. Every revolution moves the register at 12H to capture up-to 30 minutes. Longer durations of elapsed time of up to 12 hours can be read from the register at 6H. A world-leading mechanical movement Originally made in the early 1970s, the Valjoux 7750 is an updated automatic version of its hand-wound predecessors, the 7733 line from the sixties (which featured in Pinion’s R1969 limited edition chronograph). Since then, the Valjoux 7750 movement has been widely utilised by many watch companies and has become known worldwide as a simple, rugged and efficient movement. A cam-shifting action triggers the process of stopping and starting the chronograph, and the sizeable automatic winding rotor can create a characteristic known as the ‘7750 wobble’ when worn. Electroplated dial Several processes are undertaken on the dial to give its multi-contrast finish. First, the chronograph registers are milled at 12H and 6H to create two lower levels. Engine turning is applied to these to create a contrasting effect making them appear darker under differing lighting conditions. Next, subtle vertical brushing is applied to the base of the dial and circular brushing to the outer rehault ring. These are then electroplated with colour. The brushing helps with the contrasting tone of colour when viewed in different lighting conditions. Finally, the dials are gently buffed before printing commences. Once complete, a galvanic varnish is applied, sealing the elements and providing a glossy surface to the dial.
